summary: Intro discovery between Redwood (AE+SE) and Cedar Harbor (CTO/ML/Product). transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-27 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (CTO - Cedar Harbor), Miguel Alvarez (Lead ML Engineer), Sofia Tran (PM)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, this is ravi our solutions engineer, and we're excited to walk through your inference needs. how's everyone doing?

[00:18] Olivia: good thanks, quick heads up we're dialing in from boston, morning for us, appreciate the time. our goal today is to figure out which hosting path and which model family will meet latency, cost and privacy for our customer support assistant product.

[00:34] Miguel: yep, and we have pretty specific context needs — some threads go 20k tokens, and we expect to expand. multilingual is also key, english + es + fr and occasional zh. we also need tool-calling to query our internal ticket DB.

[00:50] Ravi: great, that helps. a quick primer: redwood supports hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private vpc/on-prem deployments. we typically recommend evaluating both hosted and dedicated first for throughput, then move to private if data residency or network isolation is required.

[01:10] Sofia: when you say "private", does that mean you manage the control plane or we do?

[01:18] Ravi: good question — we have two modes. for VPC private we run a customer-dedicated control plane but with customer-managed networking and optional bring-your-own-kms. for full on-prem we can ship a package — it's heavier but possible. sometimes words get swapped in notes — we call those private vs onprem options.

[01:38] Olivia: our security folks will probably insist on KMS and audit logs in-house. SSO and RBAC are musts.

[01:46] Maya: totally, we have an enterprise pack that includes sso/saml, role based access, audit trails and optional hsm integrations. we'll include the security whitepaper in the follow-up.

[02:00] Miguel: back to models — we want to avoid hallucinations when pulling ticket data and we need deterministic extraction for actions. Which open models are you seeing work best for that?

[02:15] Ravi: for structured tool-calling and low hallucination, we've had success with the latest LlamaX family for instruction-following and Mistral variants for generation quality. LlamaX-34B quantized gives you a good latency/cost balance and supports longer context when we enable the 32k profile. Mistral-30B sometimes edges out in multilingual fluency. note: some model names get mangled in transcripts — like "Lama X" — but that's the family.

[02:40] Olivia: does 32k context mean full kv cache across the request? how does that affect latency?

[02:47] Ravi: yes — to support ~32k you need optimized kv cache handling. our runtime manages kv cache across tokens and uses continuous batching; that adds memory overhead and slightly higher per-token cost but we aim to keep tail latency under target by smart routing. in dedicated mode you get predictable throughput and lower tail latency because you have reserved gpus. hosted is faster to start but can have more variability at peak.

[03:15] Miguel: and tokenization for multilingual, any gotchas? we've seen zh segmentation blow up tokens.

[03:21] Ravi: right, tokenization varies by model; some models use bpe variants that are more efficient for zh, others less so. we'll run your sample multilingual logs through tokenizers during the POC to estimate token budget.

[03:39] Sofia: what about tool-calling — do you support function-calling style webhooks or proxies?

[03:45] Maya: yes, we support streaming responses, tool/function calling patterns and structured output. the SEs usually help wire up the security-safe bridge to your ticket DB — typically via an internal proxy in the VPC, or for hosted we do a secure webhook with MTLS if you prefer.

[04:05] Miguel: we will not allow a public webhook to hit our production DB. so VPC private or a proxy seems required.

[04:12] Ravi: understood. for that we recommend the private deployment with a customer-managed VPC, or dedicated with VPC peering depending on your network posture. both support bring-your-own-kms for encryption at rest and key rotation.

[04:30] Olivia: latency targets: sub-500ms for short replies is critical for chat, but longer jobs like summarization can be async. can dedicated hit that consistently?

[04:39] Ravi: with dedicated reserved capacity you can hit consistent p95 latency targets — for the LlamaX-34B q4 profile we've seen sub-300ms token latency on NVIDIA H100-class configs for simple prompts, but it depends on prompt size and batching. we'll include realistic numbers in the benchmark report.

[04:58] Miguel: cost — how does quantization affect accuracy for our extraction tasks? we care about entity accuracy.

[05:05] Ravi: quantization can slightly affect fine-grained entity extraction, but in practice many teams use q4 or nf4 profiles and compensate with prompt engineering or small model ensembles. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload; we'll run accuracy regressions on your labeled set as part of the POC.
transcript_continued:
[05:30] Olivia: are there examples of customers doing tool-calling in a vpc with redwood?

[05:36] Maya: yes, we've done several. i'll make sure we redact a couple of case references in the security doc.

[05:44] Miguel: on streaming — do you provide partial function outputs as they arrive? we need low-latency token streaming for chat UI.

[05:51] Ravi: yes, streaming and chunked function arguments are supported. there's a small tradeoff between batch size and first-byte latency; we can tune batching to prioritize FBL (first-byte latency).

[06:06] Sofia: curious about fallback when capacity is constrained — is there automated downgrade to cheaper models?

[06:12] Ravi: smart routing lets you configure policy-based fallbacks. e.g., route to a cheaper quantized variant or lower-cost region. you'll see cost/latency tradeoffs in the console.

[06:25] Olivia: training/evals — do you support model version pinning and rollbacks? we want safety controls in production.

[06:33] Maya: yes, model versioning and rollout policies (canary, A/B, auto-fallback) are built in. Redwood Optimize also hooks evals to monitor regressions on your test prompts.

[06:45] Miguel: ok let's talk about the POC scope — we'd like 3 tasks: intent classification (short), extract entities across long context (20k-ish), and a tool-call flow to update a ticket.

[06:58] Ravi: perfect. actionable POC plan: 1) run perf/latency bench on your prompt set across LlamaX-34B q4 and Mistral-30B in hosted and dedicated configs, 2) run accuracy regressions on your labeled extraction set with q4 vs fp16, 3) demo tool-calling via a VPC proxy using a sandbox ticket DB.

[07:20] Olivia: timeline: security review will take 2 weeks maybe, procurement another 3–4. we want to kick POC early November.

[07:28] Maya: that's reasonable, we'll aim to have the bench and pricing by next friday and propose a POC kickoff week of 2026-11-08 as discussed.

[07:38] Miguel: any blockers we should flag now? our infra team will need a network diagram and minimal firewall rules for the VPC peering flow.

[07:48] Ravi: we'll produce a one-page network checklist and an onboarding playbook.

[07:55] Sofia: pricing — can you show a rough hosted per-token vs dedicated monthly commit?

[08:02] Maya: we'll include a matrix with hosted per-token, dedicated reserved GPU costs, and private licensing plus support. also notes on burst capacity and overage.

[08:12] Miguel: about compliance, we require SOC2 type II and an encryption cert — is that standard?

[08:19] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II is standard for our enterprise offering; we'll include certs and SLA language. for extra controls we can discuss custom NDAs and data handling.

[08:30] Olivia: what about regional deployments — can dedicated be provisioned in eu-west or ap-southeast? we have customers in eu.

[08:38] Ravi: yes, we support regional placement to reduce latency and meet data residency. some model builds and quant profiles are region-specific but we can coordinate.

[08:50] Sofia: last one — how often do you recommend model refreshes? we want stability but also quality improvements.

[08:58] Ravi: many teams roll models quarterly for improvements and use canary rollouts + eval harnesses to detect regressions. Redwood Optimize can automate regression alerts on your prompt-suite.

[09:12] Maya: okay great recap: we'll send pricing, security docs, network checklist; ravi will run bench and accuracy tests; olivia/miguel will share sample prompts and compliance list; schedule poc kickoff for week of 11/8.

[09:30] Olivia: sounds good, thank you both. we'll read the security pack and get the samples over early next week.

[09:38] Miguel: thanks, talk soon.

End of meeting.
